plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled branches still bare of leaves burst into fragrant blossoms with delicate, papery petals. The flowers appear while winter's chill lingers, and their sweet, spicy perfume drifts through gardens and orchards.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (roughly late January through March)
plants.location: Japan, including Mito, Atami and Kyoto, and across eastern China
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in East Asia as a symbol of perseverance, since they flower in the cold before cherry blossoms arrive. The fruit is pickled into the Japanese staple umeboshi.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding trumpets of golden yellow ring a paler yellow collar and light up woodland floors and meadows. Whole drifts of them appear together, a sign that spring is on its way.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (around late February through April)
plants.location: Western Europe, including the woodlands and meadows of England, Wales and France
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain a toxic alkaloid called lycorine, which keeps grazing animals away. Compounds from related Narcissus species are also used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Nerine sarniensis
plants.description: Spidery, wavy-edged petals glitter as if dusted with gold. Clusters of them rise on slender stalks without a leaf in sight.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, typically March to May
plants.location: Cultivated in gardens in South Africa and Australia, with wild origins in South Africa's Western Cape
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, this lily is native to South Africa. According to legend, bulbs washed ashore on Guernsey from a shipwreck and took root there.
